abstract: The MorPhiC Data Portal is the public resource for the Molecular Phenotypes of Null Alleles in Cells (MorPhiC) Consortium, which maps molecular and cellular consequences of targeted human gene inactivation. The portal integrates raw, processed and uniformly analyzed datasets from functional genomics and phenotyping assays, including bulk and single-cell RNA-seq, Perturb-seq, SLAM-seq, chromatin-accessibility profiling, and metabolomics. Release 4 (August 2026) expands the resource to perturbations of >300 genes in human induced pluripotent stem cells and derivative systems, including embryoid bodies, organoids, and differentiated models, using complementary perturbation strategies targeting DNA, RNA, and protein products. A central advance is gene-centered navigation: gene pages consolidate experimental context, perturbation strategies, cell models, datasets, phenotyping evidence, and standardized analyses, while interactive visualizations expose differential expression, enrichment, and assay-specific results. Dataset pages provide metadata, protocols, analysis summaries, and links to public repositories for raw and processed files; the portal also catalogs consortium-generated knockout cell lines. By integrating MorPhiC datasets with external annotations on essentiality, Mendelian disease associations and mammalian phenotypes, and by standardizing metadata, analysis outputs and archive submission workflows, the portal provides a reusable resource for studying human gene loss-of-function at scale. The resource is available at https://morphic.bio/data.
